newsitem.title: USA: AFL-CIO criticizes Fed's concern about wage rises.
newsitem.headline: AFL-CIO criticizes Fed's concern about wage rises.

text.p: The AFL-CIO on Wednesday criticized the Federal Reserve for worrying excessively about rising wages and warned of social and economic consequences if the central bank were to raise interest rates further in an attempt to slow the economy.

In prepared testimony to the House Banking Committee, David Smith, public policy director for the American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations, said the Fed was misguided in its belief that "modest evidence" of wage increases posed an inflation threat.
"Wage increases for American workers would be a good thing, not something to be avoid or feared. They are economically justified and badly needed," he said.
Smith said the Fed's emphasis on fighting inflation violated the spirit of the Humphrey-Hawkins law, which requires the central bank pursue both low inflation and full employment.

"Today, we have the best opportunity in a generation to realize the full employment promise of the Humphrey-Hawkins Act," Smith said. "We should not squander that chance because we fear that American workers might be getting the raise that they so rightfully deserve."
